title: The Three Little Pigs
author: Traditional
source: Public domain. Retold from the traditional English fairy tale.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time, there were three little pigs who set out into the world to build homes of their very own. Their mother hugged each of them goodbye and said,

segments.speaker: mama
segments.text: "Work hard, be clever, and take care of one another."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The first little pig did not like to work very hard. He found a farmer with a cart of straw and built himself a house of straw before lunchtime.

segments.speaker: pig-one
segments.text: "Finished already!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he said, and he spent the rest of the day napping in the sun.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The second little pig worked a little harder. He found a woodcutter with a bundle of sticks and built himself a house of sticks by suppertime.

segments.speaker: pig-two
segments.text: "Good enough!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he said, and he went inside to play.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The third little pig worked all day, and the next day, and the day after that. Brick by brick, he built a strong little house with a chimney and a heavy front door.

segments.speaker: pig-three
segments.text: "A house should keep you safe, and this one will."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he said.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now, in the woods nearby there lived a big bad wolf. He came to the house of straw, knocked on the door, and growled,

segments.speaker: wolf
segments.text: "Little pig, little pig, let me come in!"

segments.speaker: pig-one
segments.text: "Not by the hair of my chinny-chin-chin!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: cried the first pig.

segments.speaker: wolf
segments.text: "Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house in!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the wolf huffed, and he puffed, and he blew the straw house down — whoosh! The first little pig ran as fast as his trotters could carry him to his brother's house of sticks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Soon the wolf arrived at the stick house.

segments.speaker: wolf
segments.text: "Little pigs, little pigs, let me come in!"

segments.speaker: pigs
segments.text: "Not by the hairs of our chinny-chin-chins!"

segments.speaker: wolf
segments.text: "Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house in!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he huffed, and he puffed, and the stick house tumbled down — crash! The two little pigs ran all the way to their brother's house of bricks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wolf stomped up to the brick house.

segments.speaker: wolf
segments.text: "Little pigs, little pigs, let me come in!"

segments.speaker: pigs
segments.text: "Not by the hairs of our chinny-chin-chins!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: cried all three pigs together. So the wolf huffed, and he puffed, and he huffed, and he puffed — but the brick house did not move one tiny bit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wolf was not finished. He climbed onto the roof to sneak down the chimney. But the clever third pig heard his footsteps and set a big pot of vegetable soup bubbling in the fireplace. When the wolf slid down, he landed right in the hot soup — YOWCH! He shot straight back up the chimney and ran into the woods, and he never bothered the three little pigs again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After that, his two brothers helped him lay bricks, and before winter came, all three pigs had strong brick houses side by side. And every Sunday they ate soup together — vegetable soup, of course — happily ever after.
